Labels are correct hand derivations of the DBSCAN definition, but the section "boundary distance equal to epsilon" (test lines 69-75) does not discriminate: with D <= epsilon replaced by D < epsilon (line 52), computeEcosystemDBSCAN(D, 0.2, 3) still gives [0;0;0;-1;-1;-1] because point 2 (distances 0.1) is core either way. No other case has a distance equal to epsilon, so the documented inclusive rule ("lower than or equal to epsilon", header line 7) is never really tested; the "point reached twice" case also cannot fail for any labelling implementation.
suggestion: Add computeEcosystemDBSCAN(D, 0.1, 3) on the same positions: D(1,2) and D(2,3) are exactly 0.1 in binary (0.2 is 2*0.1), so with <= point 2 is core and the result is [0;0;0;-1;-1;-1]; with < every point is noise (-1). (D(4,5) = 5.1-5 = 0.0999999999999996 keeps points 4-5 non-core in both.)
